BREAKING: US nonfarm labor productivity rose at a +3.5% annualized in Q3 2026, its largest increase since Q3 2025.

This also marks its 3rd consecutive quarterly improvement.

Nonfarm business output, which excludes the impact of government spending, surged at a +3.7% annualized rate, the strongest growth rate since Q3 2025.

Hourly compensation rose at a +2.9% annualized rate.

As productivity growth outpaced hourly compensation, unit labor costs, which measure labor costs per unit of output, declined -0.7% last quarter, the first quarterly decline since Q2 2025.

This largely a product of companies investing heavily in AI, software, and equipment to improve efficiency, increase output, and contain labor expenses.

AI is catalyzing a major US productivity surge.

BREAKING: US imports of computers, computer accessories, and semiconductors surged +$12.1 billion in September, to a record $86.9 billion.

This marks the 2nd-largest monthly increase in history, following the record +$14.7 billion increase in July 2026.

Since the start of 2024, imports of computers, computer accessories, and semiconductors have more than quadrupled.

YoY, these imports rose +151%, the largest YoY increase on record, compared with peak annual growth of just +34% during the 2000 Dot-Com Boom.

Based on September's figures, these imports are now running at an annualized rate above $1.0 trillion for the first time.

US demand for technology hardware is exploding.

As for gold and Bitcoin, unfortunately they have gotten more correlated to equities lately and have joined the risk-off party in recent weeks. Both assets are 60-70% correlated to the SPX right now. https://t.co/uSILeHP2ww

BREAKING: Global crude oil in transit is up to 1.28 billion barrels, an all-time high.

This figure has surged +180 million barrels over the last several weeks.

This comes as Middle Eastern oil flows recover through the Strait of Hormuz and alternative routes, while more crude remains at sea for longer.

Ship-to-ship transfers are keeping oil aboard tankers for longer, while extended shipping routes are increasing transit times.

Meanwhile, global oil importers diversifying away from the Middle East are lengthening voyages, leaving more crude tied up aboard tankers.

As a result, more oil remains in transit rather than being readily available to refiners, tightening near-term supply despite recovering export flows.

Oil is flowing, but timely delivery is becoming the bottleneck.

BREAKING: US job openings jumped +333,000 in September, to 7.52 million, the 3rd-highest reading since November 2024.

This marks the largest monthly increase since April and the 3rd-largestsince October 2024.

The surge was led by professional and business services, which added +106,000 openings.

State and local government, excluding education, followed, with an increase of +104,000.

As a result, the ratio of job openings to unemployed workers rose to 1.06, its highest since January 2025.

There are now 414,000 more available vacancies than unemployed workers, the 2nd-largest difference since January 2025.

US labor demand appears to be recovering.

Retail demand for stocks is incredibly strong:

Retail investors purchased US equities in the 22 consecutive sessions ending November 3rd, the 3rd-longest streak since the memestock mania in 2021.

This also ranks as their 6th-longest purchasing streak since 2017.

Over this period, retail investors bought ~$33 billion in equities, their 5th-largest purchase since 2017.

This equals an average of ~$1.5 billion per trading session, and +40% above the trailing 12-month average.

Year-to-date, retail investors have purchased a record +$251 billion in equities, surpassing the previous full-year record of +$241 billion set in 2021 and marking a +134% increase from the same period last year.

Retail continues to buy the dip.
